Semiparametric Bayesian network

Source: R/dfr_llr2.R
spbn.Rd

Fits a semiparametric Bayesian network (Atienza et al., 2022) to continuous data: every node has either a linear Gaussian conditional density or a conditional kernel density estimate (CKDE) given its parents. It is the density model of dfr_llr2().

Usage

spbn(data, structure = NULL, node_types = NULL, max_parents = 4, folds = 5)

Arguments

data

A data frame or matrix of numeric variables (no missing values).

structure

Optional structure: a named list giving the parents of every variable (list(B = "A", C = c("A", "B"), A = character(0))) or a two-column matrix of arcs (from, to). NULL (default) learns it by greedy hill climbing.

node_types

Optional named character vector of node types ("lg" for linear Gaussian, "ckde" for conditional KDE). NULL (default) chooses each node's type by cross-validated log-likelihood.

max_parents

Largest number of parents of a node in the learned structure.

folds

Number of folds of the cross-validation used to choose the node types.

Value

An spbn object: the variables, their parents, node types and the fitted CPDs.

Details

Structure learning is a greedy hill climbing (arc addition, removal and reversal) with the BIC score of a Gaussian Bayesian network. The type of each node is then chosen given its parents: the type with the larger log-likelihood over folds contiguous folds (each fold scored by the CPD fitted on the other folds).

A linear Gaussian CPD is the least-squares regression of the node on its parents with the maximum likelihood variance. A CKDE CPD is f(x, pa) / f(pa), the ratio of Gaussian kernel density estimates with the bandwidth matrix of the normal reference rule, H = (4 / (d + 2))^(2 / (d + 4)) S N^(-2 / (d + 4)) (S the sample covariance of the node and its parents, d their number, N the sample size); the density of the parents uses the corresponding block of H, so the conditional density integrates to one.

The paper uses the binned version (B-SPBN), which speeds up the kernel sums by binning the data on a grid, and learns the structure and the node types together by hill climbing with a cross-validated score. Here the kernel sums are exact and the node types are chosen after the structure.

References

Atienza, D., Bielza, C. and Larrañaga, P. (2022). Semiparametric Bayesian networks. Information Sciences, 584, 564-582. doi:10.1016/j.ins.2021.10.074

See also

spbn_loglik(), dfr_llr2().

Examples

set.seed(1)
a <- stats::rnorm(500)
b <- 2 * a + stats::rnorm(500, sd = 0.5)
c <- ifelse(stats::runif(500) < 0.5, b - 3, b + 3) + stats::rnorm(500)
model <- spbn(data.frame(a, b, c))
model
#> Semiparametric Bayesian network: 3 nodes (1 linear Gaussian, 2 CKDE), 2 arcs
#>   a [lg] <- b
#>   b [ckde] <- c
#>   c [ckde] <- (none)
colMeans(spbn_loglik(model, data.frame(a, b, c)))
#>           a           b           c 
#> -0.06369788 -1.66472082 -2.70041599
